thread.title: Dow Jones Wins Again; Will FANG Stock Run Up Again? | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones Wins Again; Will FANG Stock Run Up Again? | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The major indexes posted minor gains near the lunch time hour on Wall Street. The Dow Jones industrial average led the way, rising nearly 0.5% as large caps commanded the upside in stocks today .
X At 1 p.m. ET, the Nasdaq composite and the S&P 500 lagged; the former gave back small gains and is down less than 0.1%. The Nasdaq rose 5.7% in August, then pulled 0.8% lower in September. The 500 rose around 0.1% while the Russell 2000 edged slightly lower.
Netflix ( NFLX ), one of the FANG stocks, gained nearly 0.4% in heavy trading. The online streaming video giant continues to carve the right side of a potential new base . For now, Netflix's current new basing pattern is taking on the look of a cup base . No handle has yet to form.
The base shows a normal decline from head to toe of 26.5%. Studies by IBD of big market winners during past bull markets going back to the late 1800s show that the typical correction for a good cup with handle usually does not exceed 33%.
FANG Stock Chart Analysis Recently, Netflix shares also retook the 10-week moving average, drawn in red in all IBD weekly charts. That's good. It means that institutional greed is returning.
Also, at the low of the base, at 310.93, the megacap tech did not pierce its long-term 40-week moving average. It's another sign that demand for shares among mutual funds, hedge funds, banks, insurers, college endowments and the like is still healthy.
See the 40-week moving average drawn in black in all weekly charts at MarketSmith .
Fundamentals remain strong for Netflix, despite its high long-term debt levels.
Analysts surveyed by Thomson Reuters on consensus forecast Q3 earnings to soar 134% to 68 cents a share on a 34% spike in revenue to $3.99 billion. Q4 profit is expected to lift 22% to 50 cents a share and revenue up 29% to $4.24 billion.
Dow Jones Leaders Apple ( AAPL ) helped fortify the current rally by the 30-stock blue chip index. The iPhone, iMac, Apple Watch and digital services giant was on track for a fourth gain in a row. At one point, shares rose more than 1% to mark a new all-time high of 230.
Apple has also risen more than 20%-25% since clearing a 179.04 buy point in a double-bottom base on May 4.
The big gain justifies taking at least some gains for those who bought at that correct entry . Yet those with strong conviction may decide to keep holding for potentially bigger profits.
As IBD reported on Monday, a Piper Jaffray survey of 700 U.S. iPhone owners found that demand for higher-end new iPhones may boost the company's average selling price for the popular smartphones during the next several months.
This Retail Leader Sells Off Stitch Fix ( SFIX ) gave back more than six weeks' worth of gains, free-falling more than 30% and hitting a session low of 30.38. Volume hit 19 million shares in 90 minutes of trading and bulged well past its 50-day average of 2.65 million shares.
The stock's action reaffirms a useful IBD sell rule for leading growth stocks when they break out. Consider selling at least part of your position when the post-breakout gain reaches 20% to 25%. In some cases, hold for a bigger gain when your conviction level is high; aim for larger gains of, say, 30% to 40% so long as the stock's action and the market are healthy.
The rule can also be used when a leading stock, following a breakout from a primary base such as cup with handle , double bottom or flat base , rebounds off the 10-week moving average. Stitch Fix did just that in the week ended Aug. 10, racing away from its 10-week line near 30 in higher weekly turnover vs. the prior week.
The curated online clothier late Monday reported earnings of 17 cents in the July-ended fiscal fourth quarter vs. a net loss of a penny a share a year ago. But sales grew 23% to $318.3 million, making a mild deceleration in the growth rate from gains of 26%, 25%, 24% and 29% in the prior four quarters. The top line also missed Wall Street's consensus view.
Other retailers fell but appear to be in better shape.
Ollie's Bargain Outlet ( OLLI ) dropped more than 2% to 94 but has a huge air cushion above its rising 50-day moving average. The deep discount chain cleared a flat base with a 77.60 buy point on Aug. 20, ahead of strong fiscal Q2 results.
Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ), on the watch list of IBD Leaderboard , edged more than 0.5% lower but continues to trade in a bullishly tight fashion. The cosmetics, hair and personal care products retailer is forming a new long handle on a large first-stage cup-style base. Early-stage bases tend to have a higher probability of generating successful breakouts.
Oil Rally Continues On the upside, energy firms advanced again. U.S. crude oil futures edged higher and surpassed $75 per barrel. Year to date, U.S. futures are now up more than 24%.
Small-cap Now ( DNOW ) rose as much as 3% before easing some. Shares continue to hug the rising 50-day moving average after a July 31 breakout past a 14.82 buy point in a nine-week cup with handle.
The base forms part of a long bottoming base after Now dropped as much as 76% below a 2014 peak of 37.65.
The Houston-based supplier of drilling and well completion equipment to the oil and gas machinery firm lost money from 2015 to 2017, but analysts see Now returning to the black with earnings of 31 cents a share this year.
A strong move off the 50-day or 10-week moving average would trigger a follow-on buy opportunity.
Now's RS Rating of 93 is solid, according to Stock Checkup, and it's fourth highest within IBD's oil machinery and equipment industry group.
In IBD Stocks On The Move Chegg ( CHGG ) made the Stocks On The Move table with a more-than 6% rebound in heavy trading to 29.11. The textbook and e-textbook company sharply undercut its 50-day moving average last week and is fighting to keep its long-term uptrend alive.
According to IBD's free mobile app, Chegg has notched an average EPS increase of 72% over the past three quarters. That offsets a mediocre 74 EPS Rating on a scale of 1 to 99.
Future profit growth looks solid. The Street sees earnings increasing 64% to 46 cents a share this year and up 28% to 59 cents in 2019.
